children: The pace of U.K. economic growth slowed in August to a monthly 0.1%, adding pressure on Treasury chief John Healey ahead of the Oct. 28 budget, says Joe Nellis at MHA in a note. "Although the economy has demonstrated better-than-expected resilience this year, the underlying of growth remains weak," he says. Persistent inflation has weighed on consumer confidence and spending, while higher employment costs and taxes have squeezed businesses, discouraging investment and recruitment. Rising debt-interest costs have also constrained the government's fiscal headroom. Healey should look to protect investment in artificial intelligence, while focusing on encouraging business investment, supporting employment and strengthening long-term productivity, he says. (don.forbes@wsj.com)
